{{Quote|What did the Waymancy Storm mean to the Republic? More than any conflict before or since, the Waymancy Storm found us outmatched in the technology of war.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
The '''Waymancy Storm''' was a conflict fought in [[7811 BBY]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Signatories of Waymancy]]. It originated with a disastrous first contact between the Republic and [[Warship/Legends|warships]] associated with the [[Waymancy Hollow]] region, inside which the [[Sisters of the Machinesmith]] had improved on Republic technology for a [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]]. The war was fought in the northern area of the region known as the [[Rim]], and the forces of the Signatories of Waymancy targeted both the Republic's military assets and its civilian [[Colonist/Legends|settlers]], with the Signatories' significant technological superiority leading to high losses for the Republic.

Eventually, however, the Republic achieved [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] breakthroughs while attempting to reverse-[[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] captured enemy [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]] and [[Starship/Legends|starship]] generators. The resultant technological innovations, along with the high morale among the Republic citizens, allowed it to emerge victorious over the Signatories of Waymancy, with the object known as the [[Waymancy bridal seat]] being reduced to a [[hyperspace sinkhole]] in the process. The victory in the Waymancy Storm was celebrated [[Standard year/Legends|annually]] in the Republic for at least twenty-five years, with the Republic's [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Nagratha]] delivering a speech that gave an account of the conflict at the celebration in [[7786 BBY]]. Overall, the Waymancy Storm introduced a major wave of improvements in various technologies, eventually leading to a golden age of warship construction across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|After studying our technology for a thousand years inside the Waymancy Hollow, the Sisters of the Machinesmith had improved on our designs in nearly every way.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Waymancy-EGTW.png|thumb|right|300px|The Waymancy Storm originated in the Waymancy Hollow region, which shared its name with the Waymancy system.]]
By [[7811 BBY]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had been leading [[Colonist/Legends|settlement]] efforts in the northern section of the region known as the [[Rim]]. As a result, civilians were present on such celestial bodies as [[Barenth]], [[Caursito]], and [[Upper Brightday]], which were connected to other locations via Rim-based [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|hyperspace jump beacons]] such as [[Sooncanoo Beacon]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Meanwhile, inside the [[Waymancy Hollow]] region<ref name="Author's Cut" />&mdash;which shared its name with the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]] [[Waymancy system/Legends|Waymancy system]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>&mdash;the group known as the [[Sisters of the Machinesmith]] had studied Republic technology for a [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]] leading up to that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].<ref name="Author's Cut" /> Through the [[Sif-Alulan process]],<ref name="EGTW" /> they subjected the Republic designs to a wide variety of improvements,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> resulting in the development of extremely efficient [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]]. That in turn led to the creation of [[Warship/Legends|warships]],<ref name="EGTW" /> including [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]], that could fly farther and faster than those of the Republic<ref name="Author's Cut" /> as well as [[Laser/Legends|laser]]<ref name="EGTW" /> and [[Pulse-wave blaster|pulse-wave]] [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]]&mdash;both [[Starship/Legends|starship]]-mounted and personal-scale<ref name="Author's Cut" />&mdash;that had more powerful<ref name="EGTW" /> [[Armor/Legends|armor]]-piercing capability<ref name="Author's Cut" /> and significantly faster rates of fire than the Republic's weaponry.<ref name="EGTW" />

==The war==
===The Signatories of Waymancy===
{{Quote|The Signatories of Waymancy had to be stopped. Some of their number believed in fanaticism, some believed in territorial cleansing, some believed in nothing at all beyond the cold logic of machinery. But the wholesale murder of settlers and their families? That could only be practiced by those who believed in evil.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:NorthernDependencies-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Galactic Republic fought the Signatories of Waymancy in the Northern Dependencies.]]
In 7811 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the Republic established first contact with warships associated with the Waymancy Hollow. The encounter resulted in the destruction of the former's ships by [[Space warfare/Legends|fusillades]] of the latter's laserfire.<ref name="EGTW" /> The ensuing conflict, which pitted the Republic against the [[Signatories of Waymancy]], came to be known as the Waymancy Storm and was waged in [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] of the northern Rim,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> in what was later known as the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] portion of the Inner Rim and the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="Systems" />

The forces allied with the Signatories of Waymancy included the [[Fleet/Legends|armadas]] of the [[Wives of Tingrippa]], the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Army/Legends|army]] of [[Whirl-Point-Six]], a [[Neshtabine]] nest on the celestial body [[Tantara]], and at least one raider from<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Doshan]]<ref name="IH">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> and one thug from<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet [[Muzara]].<ref name="TotJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> According to a later description by the Republic's [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Nagratha]], the beliefs of the constituent members of the Signatories included fanaticism, territorial cleansing, and the "cold logic of machinery."<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===Brutality and technological superiority===
{{Quote|Though we outnumbered our enemies a hundred to one, the frightful killing machines wielded by tyrants absent of conscience inflicted terrible losses in our ranks.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:UpperBrightday-EGTW.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Waymancy Storm saw the deaths of ten million colonists on Upper Brightday.]]
Although the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic armed forces]] outnumbered those of the Signatories a hundred to one, the superior military technology&mdash;which, per Nagratha, included "frightful killing machines"&mdash;possessed by the latter gave them a significant edge in combat that resulted in great losses for the former. The Republic found itself hard-pressed to counter the rapid-fire [[energy cannon]]s used by the mercenaries of Whirl-Point-Six, and the fleets fielded by the Wives of Tingrippa sailed between the Rim's beacons, challenging the Republic to bring forward any starship [[Hull/Legends|hull]] design that their weapons could not penetrate or muster any counterattack that their [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] could not block.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

During the Waymancy Storm, the Signatories of Waymancy targeted both the Republic's armed forces and its settlers, in the process ravaging the worlds of the northern Rim. As the war progressed, the actions of the Signatories became progressively [[Blood/Legends|bloodier]]. The Republic's enemy [[Fire/Legends|incinerated]] the lands of the settlers on Upper Brightday, resulting in the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of ten million colonists. At Barenth, the Republic mounted a [[Defense of Barenth|defense]] that allowed for a near-complete evacuation of the<ref name="Author's Cut" /> world's<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> civilian population, although an entire Republic [[Battle group/Legends|battle group]] and its personnel was lost in the process. And when the [[Fortieth Flotilla]] of the Republic underwent a risky attempt to boost the shields of its vessels at Sooncanoo Beacon, the attempt failed, leaving the [[Flotilla/Legends|flotilla]] to float powerless in [[Realspace/Legends|space]], where the enemy subsequently [[Massacre at Sooncanoo Beacon|massacred]] every crewmember of the unit.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===Republic's response===
{{Quote|Liberating the northern Rim was never in question. All Republic residents are equally valued, whether they make their homes on Coruscant or on Caursito. After mourning our losses, we citizens rose up as one to deliver our response.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Axum25200BBY-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The scientific breakthroughs made on Axum proved vital to the Republic's war effort.]]
According to Nagratha, the Republic placed a high priority on the welfare of its far-flung settlements and, accordingly, liberating the holdings seized by the Signatories of Waymancy. After a mourning period for the losses suffered on the northern Rim, the Republic experienced an upwelling of determination on the part of its citizens to respond to the Signatories' actions. The Republic's military saw an increase in the number of volunteers, and its [[Factory/Legends|factories]] in the Expansion Region busily produced [[armored galleon]]s and [[Crawler (vehicle)|crawler mechs]] for the war effort. The high morale of the Republic's [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] was also demonstrated on the battlefield, such as during their refusal to desert the fortifications at the<ref name="Author's Cut" /> planet<ref name="CSWE Paig">{{CSWECite|III|5|Paig}}</ref> [[Paig]] or during a fleet element's actions at the [[Second Battle of Brightday]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Republic [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and codebreakers&mdash;including the group known as the [[Squill Sifters/Legends|Squill Sifters]], of which [[Nagratha's mother]] was a member&mdash;placed intense effort into interpreting large quantities of intercepted enemy data. At some point, the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] also captured at the astronomical object [[Sif-Alula]] a quantity of the Signatories' weapons and starship generators. Subsequently, technologists at a Republic [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] on<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Axum]] attempted to reverse-[[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] the technology, achieving [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] breakthroughs in the process.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===Endgame===
{{Quote|And you did it. We&mdash;the Republic&mdash;did it.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:RocketJumper-GAW.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Republic rocket-jumpers became legendary for fighting in the Waymancy Storm.]]
Armed with newly improved offensive and defensive capabilities, the Republic forces eventually managed to turn the tide of the war in their favor. At the celestial body [[Immalia]], the Republic [[cannonship]] ''[[Squintpipe]]'', equipped with an experimental [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] and [[energy skin]], ended the [[Bombardment of Immalia|orbital bombardment]] the Signatories were carrying out and drove away their warships. Republic agents, including [[Chief sergeant|Chief Sergeant]] [[Saens Sukko]], scaled a [[Mittoblade's magnetic cliff|magnetic cliff]] on the astronomical object [[Mittoblade/Legends|Mittoblade]], where Sukko was instrumental in [[Collapse of the Clowse Glowstack|destroying]] the enemy structure known as the [[Clowse Glowstack]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The Republic's [[ROCKET|rocket pack]]&ndash;equipped<ref name="TotJC" /> [[Rocket-Jumper Elite Advance Unit]] also fought bravely in the Waymancy Storm,<ref name="Author's Cut" /> with it eventually becoming one of the conflicts in which their participation made the unit legendary.<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> One of the actions carried out by the rocket-jumpers was the [[Rout on Tantara|rout]] of the Tantara nest. Ultimately, the Republic forces committed to a final push that saw the reduction of the object known as the [[Waymancy bridal seat]] to a [[hyperspace sinkhole]] and, eventually, overall victory in the Waymancy Storm on what Nagratha characterized as a "solemn, glorious" [[Standard day/Legends|day]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Aftermath==
===Remembrance of victory===
{{Quote|Victory in the Waymancy Storm has been celebrated every year since that solemn, glorious day 25 years removed. It will be remembered long after I have left office and long after all of our lives have passed into history.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Uglykotoricon.svg|thumb|left|300px|The Galactic Republic (emblem pictured) celebrated its victory in the Waymancy Storm annually for at least twenty-five years.]]
The Republic celebrated the victory in the Waymancy Storm each year for at least twenty-five years. At a commemorative service on the [[25th anniversary of Victory in the Waymancy Storm]] in [[7786 BBY]], Supreme Chancellor Nagratha delivered a speech that was also transmitted to other Republic worlds. Nagratha acknowledged the critical role the veterans attending the service, as well as their fallen fellow soldiers, had played in the outcome of the war and thanked them for their service.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

In the speech, the Supreme Chancellor gave a brief account of the conflict, focusing on the threat posed to the Republic's citizens by the Signatories of Waymancy, whom Nagratha characterized as "tyrants absent of conscience" and as a "force of evil" that unleashed "atrocities" upon the Republic, and the challenges faced by the Republic in opposing them. The Republic's leader viewed the war as a "necessary" effort with the goal of stopping the Signatories' actions. Nagratha invoked the Rim colonies that had been targeted during the Waymancy Storm and had since then become thriving worlds and members of a Republic that was steadily growing in defiance of the threat formerly posed by the Signatories. The Supreme Chancellor further expressed their conviction that the victory in the war would still be commemorated long after the lives of all the attendees of the service had passed.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===Technological innovation===
{{Quote|No, we would never have given up. But without the scientific breakthroughs made on Axum, the cost in Republic lives would have been far greater.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Turbolaser-dt1.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Among other technology innovations, the Waymancy Storm introduced improvements to turbolasers (a turbolaser pictured).]]
According to Nagratha, during the Waymancy Storm, the technology used by the Republic was outclassed by that of its enemy more than in any of the previous or subsequent conflicts in the Republic's<ref name="Author's Cut" /> tens of millennia&ndash;long history.<ref name="EGTW" /> The Supreme Chancellor speculated that, while the Republic would not have been defeated without the technological innovations brought forth on Axum, it would have suffered a much higher number of casualties.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The Waymancy Storm ushered in a major wave of innovations in technology. After the Republic emerged victorious in the conflict, the Sif-Alulan process was reverse-engineered, and in the [[7700s BBY]], master crafter [[Lyns Skutroo]] unveiled the [[squintpipe process]] for improving the power generators used aboard starships. The subsequent improvements in energy weaponry resulted in rapid-fire [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] briefly outmatching all available defense technologies, with tacticians searching for stronger hull armor and retiring the use of larger [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] in favor of overwhelming amounts of smaller [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]]. Further refinements of the squintpipe process in the [[7500s BBY]], however, led to improved shielding technologies, and overall the process led to a golden age of warship construction across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and the eventual re-emergence of the combat use of capital ships.<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|<nowiki />''[&hellip;]'' the Waymancy Storm was created by Dan Wallace for ''Galaxy at War''. Dan wrote a cool account of the Waymancy Storm for me&mdash;complete with his usual wonderfully evocative names&mdash;but it too wound up on the cutting-room floor.|Jason Fry, on the writing process of ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''|<ref name="Fry3">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/21215590247/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-3|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 3}}</ref>}}
The Waymancy Storm was introduced in a section of the [[2009]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook ''[[Galaxy at War]]''<ref name="GaW" /> authored by [[Daniel Wallace]].<ref name="Fry3" /> An [[in-universe]] account of the Waymancy Storm was originally meant to be included in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the Wallace-authored section that would have mentioned the conflict was cut before the book's release. That section was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various content cut from the book.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
